stories.summary: Rescue teams evacuate villagers by boat in Sheikhupura, Pakistan, after monsoon floods submerged homes and left communities without basic supplies.

stories.title: Zelenskyy and Trump hold closed-door White House talks on war in Ukraine
stories.summary: Since returning to office early last year, Trump has halted direct US arms deliveries to Kyiv in favour of a programme allowing European countries to buy weapons for Ukraine.

stories.title: Trump and Netanyahu hold first face-to-face talks since their 'disagreement' on the Iran war
stories.summary: The meeting was the eighth between Trump and Netanyahu since the US president returned to office in early 2025 and came ahead of elections in Israel and US midterms later this year.

stories.title: Keiko Fujimori takes office as Peru's president, vowing to end decade of instability
stories.summary: The Popular Force leader becomes Peru's first female president, returning Fujimorism to power after 26 years. She is due to deliver her inaugural address and unveil her cabinet. King Felipe VI attended the ceremony in Lima.

stories.title: Rescuers scramble to locate survivors as death toll climbs to 13 after powerful quake hits southwestern Japan
stories.summary: Dozens more remain trapped underneath the rubble as authorities race against the clock to save as many people as possible during the critical 72 hour rescue period. The tremor is the most powerful to hit the region in 10 years since a 7.0 magnitude quake recorded in 2016.

stories.title: Japan earthquake shakes Kumamoto newsroom as staff shelter under desks
stories.summary: Footage shows newsroom staff taking cover as a magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck Kumamoto in southwestern Japan, killing 13 people.

stories.title: Wisconsin tornado leaves homes damaged and streets covered in debris
stories.summary: Residents in Menasha, Wisconsin, survey tornado damage as crews assess destroyed homes, fallen trees and damaged power lines after the storm.

stories.title: FIFA boss Infantino takes aim at World Cup critics
stories.summary: In a strongly worded open statement, FIFA President Gianni Infantino has hit out at those he says were too "consumed by hate and criticism" to enjoy the tournament. Infantino brushed off a number of corruption concerns.

stories.title: Shots fired near US consulate in Canada for second time in four months
stories.summary: No one was injured and no suspects have been identified in connection to shooting near Toronto compound, police say Shots were fired near the US consulate in Toronto early on Monday but no one was injured in the second shooting near the diplomatic compound in four months. “Officers heard a firearm being discharged in the area,” and “a white sedan was seen fleeing the scene”, Toronto police said on X. Continue reading...

stories.title: Pinochet-era soldier jailed for killing folk singer Víctor Jara 53 years ago
stories.summary: Nelson Haase Mazzei was sentenced for murdering Jara in 2023, but fled from authorities in Chile More than 50 years after the murder of the Chilean folk singer Víctor Jara , the last man wanted in connection with his death has been tracked down and brought to justice. Nelson Haase Mazzei, a retired colonel, fled from authorities in 2023 after he and six other retired soldiers were sentenced in absentia for murdering Jara and another man. Continue reading...

stories.title: Who has the momentum in the Russia-Ukraine war? – video explainer
stories.summary: Since Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, the war in Ukraine has changed dramatically. The Guardian's Luke Harding looks at who has the advantage in the war now and how Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy's strategy has shifted Continue reading...

stories.title: What do the heatwaves in Europe and North America tell us about our future? | Fiona Katauskas
stories.summary: The signs are there See more of Fiona Katauskas’s cartoons here Continue reading...

stories.title: Car ramming attacks: Why do they keep happening?
stories.summary: Cars are being used as weapons, to ram, kill and maim innocent people. The reasons why are not always clear, nor are solutions to preventing such attacks.

stories.title: 'Amnesia' about measles risk and low vaccination rates have helped US infections grow
stories.summary: The latest US data show measles cases from January to mid-July 2026 totaled more than all cases in 2025. Experts blame a fall in vaccination and warn that people have forgotten measles can be life-threatening.

stories.title: Germany: Islamist terror attack on Berlin Pride parade triggers political debate
stories.summary: Following the terrorist attack on Berlin's Pride parade, the Christopher Street Day parade, politicians and security experts are demanding consequences.

stories.title: German Chancellor Merz completes cabinet reshuffle
stories.summary: After days of confusion, Chancellor Friedrich Merz has reshuffled his cabinet. Conservative politicians fear that this will not help with the prospects in the upcoming state elections.

stories.title: Seattle police say shooting incident at food festival over the weekend may have been gang related
stories.summary: The shooting incident killed three people, one of them now identified as one of the shooters, and injured four others, including a two-year-old boy, according to Seattle police.

stories.title: High-wire artists walk cables across Jerusalem's Hinnom Valley
stories.summary: Four high-wire artists rehearse above Jerusalem's Hinnom Valley ahead of the 65th Israel Festival, paying tribute to Philippe Petit's 1987 crossing.

stories.title: White House prepares for high-stakes talks with Zelenskyy and Netanyahu
stories.summary: The meetings will showcase Washington's foreign policy balancing act as it tries to broker peace in Ukraine, despite being the instigator of military action in the Middle East.

stories.title: MoD cancels army training in Kenya over powers to prosecute British soldiers
stories.summary: September exercise called off after Kenya raises concerns over funding and jurisdiction for criminal offences The British army has been forced to cancel training for its troops in Kenya after the Kenyan government refused to ratify a bilateral defence agreement. While the UK government wanted to renew the existing agreement, Kenyan lawmakers had sought changes to give local authorities greater powers to hold British soldiers accountable for any offences committed in the country. Continue reading

stories.title: Two Russian men jailed in Angola for terrorism and spying
stories.summary: The men were convicted over alleged plan to stage coup and organise deadly demonstrations over fuel prices last year Two Russian men have been found guilty by an Angolan court of terrorism and spying after being accused of planning a coup and helping to organise deadly demonstrations in the southern African country last year. stories.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party protest victory signals trouble ahead for Modi
stories.summary: Ally forced to resign, with opposition parties reinvigorated and strongman leader’s grip over media channels rocked Even the night before Narendra Modi accepted the resignation of his education minister, India’s prime minister appeared confident that the largest mass uprising to take place in his 12 years in power would do little to rattle his government. stories.title: Uganda begins emergency food handouts after 19 die from hunger
stories.summary: Government move follows months of drought and crop failures in Karamoja, with 1.5m people facing malnutrition Uganda has launched emergency food relief distribution after at least 19 deaths from hunger were reported in an area of prolonged drought in the east of the country. A crisis has been building in the Karamoja region of Uganda as crops have failed without the season’s expected rains, leaving the region’s 1.5 million people facing acute food shortages and rising malnutrition. Continue read

stories.title: Firefighters in Spain and France battle raging wildfires – video
stories.summary: Footage shows the extent of the devastation caused by wildfires in Cenicientos, in the Madrid region of Spain, on Friday. Members of Spain's military emergency unit sought to contain the blazes in the Madrid region and in Cuevas de Cañart in the country's north-east. In France, dozens of firefighters battled flames threatening homes around the towns of Saumos and Sainte-Hélène in the south-west as a wildfire swept the nearby forest. stories.title: Spain wildfire burns 'out of extinguishing capacity' as fires engulf parts of Europe – video
stories.summary: A wildfire burning in Spain's eastern Castellón province has grown beyond firefighting capacity, the Valencia regional government has said. Wildfires in Spain and France have driven more than 300,000 people to flee their homes and holiday accommodation. France has been worst affected by the wildfires, with an approximate area of 42,000 hectares (103,800 acres) burned so far by the flames Continue reading...

stories.title: Weather tracker: Why Europe’s wildfires are proving so fierce and difficult to stop
stories.summary: Wind and record-breaking heat are fuelling the continent’s explosive fire season, with Spain and France among worst hit Explainer: what is a ‘fire cloud’, and how have they worsened wildfires in Europe? Europe wildfires live – latest updates A combination of an unusually wet winter, very low rainfall since spring and repeated record-breaking summer heatwaves is likely to explain why wildfires have ignited, spread and resisted control so readily across France and Spain in recent days . stories.title: Eco wins: Cities, creatures, and tech are saving the day
stories.summary: From an AI-powered cute little pangolin, heat mapping to cool down cities and animals reducing wildfire risks by doing their thing, these real-world climate hacks are helping communities stay ahead of a changing planet.

stories.title: Could 'mesh networks' help overcome authoritarians' internet blocks?
stories.summary: In authoritarian countries, the state is often either monitoring online communications or has the ability to shut them down in a political crisis. But there are other ways that activists can keep in touch.

stories.title: Germany news: Industry hemorrhaging 15,000 jobs a month
stories.summary: Industry boss Tanja Gönner says the situation is critical but offers opportunity. Meanwhile, politicians head to the Bayreuth Festival and security services warn of racist fight clubs. Follow DW for the latest.

stories.title: Tour de France final stage shortened due to wildfires
stories.summary: Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.

stories.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
stories.summary: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

stories.title: Serbia's LGBTQ+ community faces 'epidemic of violence'
stories.summary: Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have never been higher. The attacks are part of a larger shift in society targeting marginalized people.

stories.title: WAFCON 2026: What you need to know
stories.summary: Several months after it was supposed to start and with more teams than first planned, WAFCON 2026 is finally set to begin. The hosts want a maiden title while a tournament outsider have one of its best players.

stories.title: Berlin Pride: Latest in string of deadly vehicle attacks
stories.summary: The attack at a Berlin Pride event is only the most recent incident on a long list where vehicles were used as weapons. The US, Canada, and China also saw similar attacks in recent years.

stories.title: Berlin Pride attack: What we know so far
stories.summary: On Saturday, a vehicle drove into a crowd near a Christopher Street Day celebration in what is being regarded as an attack on the LGBTQ+ community. The main suspect has since been confronted and shot dead.

stories.title: Berlin Pride ramming: Police shoot suspect dead
stories.summary: Police said the suspect was shot dead in an operation, after the incident was classified as an "Islamist terrorist" attack. One person was killed and several others injured in the attack.

stories.title: EU rejects suspending biometric border controls despite 20 ‘difficult spots’
stories.summary: Officials admit new post-Brexit EES system is ‘not perfect’, as airports and airlines voice fears over delays The EU has rejected calls by airports and airlines to suspend the implementation of new fingerprinting and facial recognition border controls even though it admits there are “20 difficult spots” with queue chaos. stories.title: Spain and Gibraltar celebrate as border fence falls after signing of ‘historic deal’
stories.summary: Treaty came into effect at midnight, eliminating border controls on land frontier with British overseas territory Europe live – latest updates UK politics live – latest updates Spain and Gibraltar are celebrating the fall of the last frontier fence in western Europe after the signing of a post-Brexit deal that brings an end to border checks for residents, tourists and the thousands of Spanish workers who cross into the British overseas territory every day. stories.title: France and UK to increase staffing at border controls in effort to avert travel chaos
stories.summary: Disruption at Channel crossings expected to rise amid new fingerprint and facial recognition checks France and the UK have agreed to increase staffing at border controls in response to warnings of travel chaos caused by new fingerprinting and facial recognition checks. stories.summary: European leaders have made positive noises about the new UK PM, but he is likely to face the same restrictions as Starmer Andy Burnham is unknown in Brussels, but that will soon change.
